title: Session 2: Subordinating Conjunctions
summary: The most common subordinating conjunctions — although, though, even though, when, while, if, unless, since, once, until, because, so that and that — what each one means, and the comma rule for DC, IC and IC DC. Plus a FANBOYS review.

blocks.title: By the end of this session you can …
items: Explain what a subordinating conjunction does to a clause
Use the most common subordinating conjunctions with the right meaning
Use a comma after a dependent clause at the start (DC, IC) and no comma in IC DC
Never use although + but, or because + so, in the same sentence

blocks.title: Remember from Session 1
items: FANBOYS = for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so.
**IC, FANBOYS IC** → comma before the conjunction: It was late, so we took a taxi.
Two verbs, one subject → no comma: She ate quickly and left.

blocks.text: 2. What does a subordinating conjunction do?

A subordinating conjunction goes at the start of a clause and makes it **dependent**. A **dependent clause (DC)** has a subject and a verb, but it **cannot stand alone** — it needs an independent clause (IC) to complete the meaning.

headers: Dependent clause (DC) — not a sentence on its own

blocks.title: A DC alone is a fragment
items: ✗ Because it was raining. (What happened? The idea is not complete.)
✓ We stayed inside because it was raining. ✓ Because it was raining, we stayed inside.

rows: although, though, even though, while, whereas
**Although** the test was hard, she finished it.
when, while, before, after, until, since, once, as soon as
**When** the bell rang, the students left.
We stayed home **because** it was snowing.
**If** you practise every day, you will improve.
She saved money **so that** she could buy a laptop.
Scientists believe **that** the climate is changing.

blocks.title: ALTHOUGH · THOUGH · EVEN THOUGH = contrast
items: The two ideas are opposite: Although he was ill, he went to school.
Though means the same and is slightly less formal. Even though is stronger (more surprising).
✗ Although it was cold, but we went swimming. — never use **although + but** together. Choose one: Although it was cold, we went swimming. / It was cold, but we went swimming.

blocks.title: WHEN vs WHILE (time)
items: When = at that moment (often a short action): When the phone rang, I answered it.
While = during a longer action (often with the past continuous): While I was cooking, the phone rang.

blocks.title: WHILE · WHEREAS = contrast between two facts
items: While can also compare two different things: My brother loves football, **while** I prefer tennis.
Whereas is used only for this comparison: Cairo is hot and dry, **whereas** London is cool and wet.
These two are the one place where we often put a comma in IC DC, because the two facts are being compared.

blocks.title: SINCE: two meanings
items: **Time** (from a point in the past until now) → use the present perfect: I have lived here **since** I was five.
**Reason** (= because): **Since** the shop was closed, we went home.

blocks.title: ONCE · UNTIL · AS SOON AS
items: Once = after / as soon as: **Once** you finish the test, hand in your paper.
Until = up to that time: Wait here **until** I come back.
With until, once, when, as soon as, before, after, if, use the **present** tense for the future: ✗ until I will come back ✓ until I come back.

blocks.title: IF · UNLESS = condition
items: If you leave now, you will catch the bus.
Unless = if … not: **Unless** you leave now, you will miss the bus. (= If you don't leave now …)
✗ Unless you don't leave now — unless is already negative.

blocks.title: BECAUSE · SO THAT
items: Because gives the reason: She was late **because** her car broke down.
So that gives the purpose (the aim): She left early **so that** she would not be late.
✗ Because she was tired, so she slept. — never **because + so** in one sentence.

blocks.title: THAT
items: That starts a clause that acts like a noun, often after verbs such as think, believe, know, say, show, suggest: The results show **that** the plan worked.
In academic writing, keep that after show, suggest, argue, believe: Research suggests **that** sleep improves memory.

rows: **Although it was late**, we kept working.
We kept working **although it was late**.

blocks.title: Easy way to remember
items: If the sentence **starts** with the subordinating conjunction, put a comma where the dependent clause ends.
If the conjunction is in the **middle**, you usually need no comma (except whereas / while when you compare two facts).

blocks.title: FANBOYS or subordinating conjunction?
items: It was cold, **but** we went out. = **Although** it was cold, we went out. Same meaning, different structure.
It was late, **so** we took a taxi. = **Because** it was late, we took a taxi.
Use one joining word for one link — not two.

items.q: Choose: ___ she was very tired, she finished the essay. (Although / Because)
Choose: Stay inside ___ the rain stops. (until / since)
Choose: I have known Omar ___ we were six. (since / while)
Choose: ___ you hurry, you will be late. (If / Unless)
Choose: She studied hard ___ she could get a scholarship. (so that / because)
Choose: ___ I was walking home, I saw an accident. (While / Once)
Add the comma if needed: When the film ended we went home.
items.a: When the film ended, we went home. (DC, IC)

items.q: Add the comma if needed: We went home when the film ended.
Correct: Although the hotel was expensive, but the rooms were small.
items.a: Although the hotel was expensive, the rooms were small. (or: The hotel was expensive, but the rooms were small.)

items.q: Correct: Because it was raining. We stayed at home.
items.a: Fragment. ✓ Because it was raining, we stayed at home.

items.q: Correct: I will call you when I will arrive.
items.a: I will call you when I arrive.

items.q: Rewrite with **although**: The task was difficult, but we finished it.
items.a: Although the task was difficult, we finished it.

questions.q: What does a subordinating conjunction do to a clause?

c: Because the road was closed, we turned back.
We turned back because the road was closed.

questions.q: ___ he trained hard, he lost the race.
You will fail ___ you study. (= if you do not study)
She whispered ___ the baby would not wake up.

c: The students left, when the bell rang.
When, the bell rang the students left.
When the bell rang the students left.
When the bell rang, the students left.
We waited until the rain stopped.
We waited, until the rain stopped.
Until the rain stopped we waited.
We waited until, the rain stopped.
Although it was late, but we kept working.
It was late, although but we kept working.
Although it was late but we kept working.
Although it was late, we kept working.
Because he was ill, so he stayed at home.
Because he was ill, he stayed at home.
Because he was ill. He stayed at home.
He was ill, because so he stayed at home.

questions.q: ___ I was reading, the lights went out. (a longer action)
Choose the correct verb: Wait here until the teacher ___.
My sister is quiet, ___ my brother is very loud. (comparing two facts)
The report shows ___ sales increased last year.
___ you finish the first draft, check every comma. (= as soon as)
